Elara Dawn — Album 3.5: House of Miracles

Known By Heart

"Not by every fragment you can see"

[Verse 1 — intimate, steady, grounded] You can trace every reaction Name the patterns as they form You can map the way I answer Every shift before the storm

You can study every version You can follow every thread

But I am not the sum of everything

You think you’ve read

[Pre-Chorus — quiet, anchored] You see clearly That much is true

But seeing something

Does not give it ownership of you

[Chorus — calm, grounded, immovable] I am known by heart Not by every fragment you can see Not by every version You’ve tried to take from me

You can name the shape I’m shifting You can watch the way I start

But I am more than what you measure

I am known by heart

Known by heart Known by heart

[Verse 2 — stronger, steady defiance without aggression] You can watch the way it fractures Watch identity divide Watch the moment something slips

When doubt replaces what was inside

But there is something underneath it That you cannot reorganize

Something deeper than reflection

That does not rely on eyes

[Pre-Chorus] You collapse What you can hold

But not everything that matters

Can be controlled

[Chorus] I am known by heart Not by what you think you see Not by every version You collect inside of me

You can blur the lines around me You can pull the world apart

But I still remain

What you can’t take from the heart

Known by heart Known by heart

[Bridge — “infantry” stronger now, identity reinforcement] (Voices layered — not soft now, stronger, unified)

You are still you You are still you

(Elara) Even now

(Voices) Even now

You are still you

[Build — tightening, identity locking in]

[Final Chorus — grounded power, not explosive] I am known by heart Even when the image breaks Even when the mirror shifts Even when the pattern shakes

You can take what can be seen You can pull the world apart

But you will never rewrite

What is held inside the heart

Known by heart Known by heart

[Outro — quiet, steady, final] You see me

…

but you don’t own me
